title: How to connect multiple Slack workspaces to Claude, Codex & Cursor
summary: Connect multiple Slack workspaces to Claude, Codex, or Cursor and start using them in the same conversation.
body_markdown:
Your team’s discussions might live in one Slack workspace, while conversations with clients happen in another. However, Claude’s official Slack connector[only supports one workspace per account](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/44243) .


[Nango](https://nango.dev/) lets you connect multiple Slack workspaces to Claude via its Management MCP. It’s free and should take less than 5 minutes.


The[free plan includes 10 connections](https://nango.dev/pricing) , so you can connect up to 10 different Slack workspaces.


**Update (October 2026):** Some Claude users report multi-account support for Google connectors; Slack support remains unconfirmed. With support for 1,000+ APIs, Nango lets you connect multiple Slack workspaces and other app accounts once, then reuse them across Claude, Codex, and Cursor through one MCP connection. You can also share a connect link so someone with the necessary Slack permissions can authorize access without creating a Nango account.


## Step 1: Add a new Nango integration


[Create a free Nango account](https://app.nango.dev/signup) or log in. Select **dev** in the top-left environment menu, then go to **Integrations → Set up new integration** and search for Slack. Select **Slack** with the **OAuth 2** label.


Keep **Nango-managed OAuth app** selected and click **Create** .


Nango’s managed app saves you from creating and setting up your own app in Slack’s developer portal. Nango provides similar managed apps for 70+ popular APIs, including Salesforce and Google.


## Step 2: Connect multiple Slack workspaces


Go to **Connections → Add test connection** and select the **Slack** integration you just created.


1. Click **Authorize** , then **Connect** in the Link Slack Account window.
2. Select your first workspace in Slack’s workspace picker. We use **Kerneldev** in this example.
3. If Slack asks for a **Channel for webhook** , choose a channel, such as` #general` .
4. Review the permissions, click **Allow** , then click **Finish** when Nango confirms the connection.


You’ll see a new Slack entry on Nango’s **Connections** page. Repeat these steps for your second workspace, choosing it in Slack’s workspace picker before clicking **Allow** . Our second workspace is **Nango Tutorial** .


After authorization, both workspaces appear as separate connections:


Repeat for any other workspaces you want to connect.


**Don’t have access to a workspace or see “You are not authorized to install”?** Return to **Add test connection** , select Slack, click **Share connect link** , and copy the link. Send it to a workspace owner or app manager.


They can sign in to Slack and authorize the app without a Nango account. The new connection then appears in your **Connections** list. Links expire after 30 minutes.


## Step 3: Connect Nango to Claude, Codex, Cursor, and others


### Claude


1. Open **Customize → Connectors → Discover** in Claude and search for **Nango** . You can also open the[Nango connector listing](https://claude.ai/customize/connectors/id/mcp-nango-dev) directly.
2. Select **Nango** (described as “Manage Nango integrations”) and click **Connect to Claude** .
3. Sign in to the Nango account containing your Slack connections and approve access.
4. Start a new conversation. Open **+ → Connectors** in the message box and enable Nango. Restart Claude if the connector doesn’t appear.


On a Team or Enterprise plan, ask your organization owner to enable Nango if it isn’t available.


### Codex, Cursor, and other agents


Follow[Nango’s setup instructions for your agent](https://nango.dev/docs/getting-started/coding-agent-setup) . The same Slack connections are available once you connect it to Nango; you don’t need to authorize each workspace again.


## Step 4: Start using Claude to access multiple Slack workspaces


Start with a simple prompt:


> List names of all Slack workspaces connected via Nango.


Allow Claude’s requests to look up your connected workspaces. The result should include both, along with any other Slack workspaces you’ve connected before.


Behind the scenes, Claude uses Nango’s Management MCP to find your connections and choose from 10,000+ pre-built tools. MCP usage is included in the free plan, subject to its monthly limits.


### Read messages and send a reply across workspaces


To let Claude read a channel’s messages, add Nango to that channel in Slack: open the channel’s details, choose **Agents and apps → Add agents and apps** , and click **Add** next to **Nango** . Repeat for each channel you want Claude to read.


Now ask Claude to read a discussion in **Nango Tutorial’s #all-nango-tutorial** channel and post a message in **Kerneldev’s #general** channel asking for the customer’s preferred AWS region and security requirements. The prompt below matches the screenshot and explicitly approves posting the message. Replace the workspace and channel names, integration ID, environment, and action names with those in your own setup:


> Using Nango, read the discussion about hosting our app in a customer’s AWS account in Nango Tutorial’s #all-nango-tutorial channel. Then send one short message in Kerneldev’s #general asking for the customer’s preferred AWS region and security requirements before proposing a deployment plan. You have my approval to post that message.


> Use the slack-ynfm integration in dev and the existing get-conversation-history-compat and send-message-compat actions.


To search messages across an entire workspace, follow Nango’s[additional Slack setup](https://nango.dev/docs/api-integrations/slack/slack-user-access-tokens) .


## Connecting 1,000+ apps to your agent with Nango


Nango is a customer-facing agent integrations platform that supports[1,000+ APIs](https://nango.dev/api-integrations) and 10,000+ pre-built agent tools. Add Gmail, Google Calendar, Salesforce, or other accounts in Nango. New connections are available through the Nango connector you’ve already installed in Claude, Codex, or Cursor.


Behind the scenes, Nango manages authorization and keeps connections working as credentials expire. Webhooks and events let your agents react to new messages or updated customer records, while data syncing keeps their information up to date. Coding agents including Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor can build custom integrations on Nango when you need something beyond the available tools.
